query: For titanium alloys used as structural materials, formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could increase surface hardness and wear resistance. Specify the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to the untreated alloy, the service or test conditions under which the effect should hold, prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with clear results that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a low-temperature plasma nitriding process to titanium alloys will form a dense TiN surface layer that increases surface hardness and wear resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: A commercial titanium alloy with a typical microstructure and minimal pre-existing surface nitride phases.
generation.intervention: Subject the alloy to plasma nitriding under a controlled nitrogen atmosphere at a relatively low temperature (around 450°C) for a designated duration (e.g., 2 hours).
generation.conditions: The enhanced surface properties should be maintained during service or testing under moderate sliding loads and speeds at room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a thin, continuous, and dense titanium nitride (TiN) surface layer.
generation.mechanism: Nitrogen diffuses into the titanium surface during the plasma nitriding process, leading to the in-situ formation of hard TiN precipitates. These nitride phases inhibit dislocation motion and act as an effective barrier against abrasive and adhesive wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated titanium alloys, the treated alloy is expected to show an increase in surface hardness by roughly 30–50% and a corresponding reduction in wear rate under similar testing conditions.
generation.baseline: Untreated titanium alloy exhibiting standard surface hardness and wear characteristics.
generation.boundary: Improvements are expected under moderate mechanical loads and ambient temperature conditions; under extreme conditions (very high loads or temperatures), the integrity of the nitrided layer may degrade, potentially limiting the benefits.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of improvement and the long-term stability of the TiN layer under cyclic or high-stress conditions remain to be quantified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of titanium alloy samples: one set will undergo the specified plasma nitriding process, while the control set will remain untreated. Conduct a series of nanoindentation tests to measure surface hardness and pin-on-disk wear tests under identical (moderate load and room temperature) conditions.
measurements: Wear rate (via pin-on-disk or equivalent wear testing)
Detailed surface characterization (using SEM/TEM to confirm the presence, continuity, and thickness of the TiN layer)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the plasma nitrided samples do not demonstrate a statistically significant increase (>10% improvement) in surface hardness and reduction in wear rate compared to the untreated samples, or if the TiN layer is not observed or is non-uniform as determined by surface characterization, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The third way is to modify its surface structure through surface engineering technology [], such as carburizing, nitriding and boronizing. For example, with Ni45(CoCrFe)40(AlTi)15 surface nitriding [], AlN, CrN and TiN phases are formed on the surface, effectively increasing the surface hardness of the alloy from 8.8 GPa to 14.9 GPa. Furthermore, the utilization of shot peening, laser remelting and various other technologies also have the potential to enhance the surface characteristics of HEAs [,]. Al, Ti and Cr are widely used in alloys because of their effects on microstructure, strengthening and oxidation resistance. V is commonly used to improve friction and wear properties because its atomic size deforms the crystal structure of BCC and FCC alloys. As a lightweight alloy, the mechanical properties and corrosion resistance of the HEA of AlCrVTi have been studied, but the effect of the content of Nb on the wear resistance of the HEA has not been studied [,,,]. In this paper, AlCrTiVNbx (x = 0.3, 0.4, 0.5) HEAs were prepared by vacuum arc melting and annealed at 1000 °C for 2 h to investigate the changes in microstructure and mechanical properties before and after annealing.
